I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is the safest way for me to earn grain, use the seasons fully, and avoid taking on too much risk at my age. I do not want a complicated planting plan with too many crops, because that means more labor, more watching, and more chances to lose money. I will sow winter wheat first, then follow it with summer maize on the same land. I will use improved or hybrid seed because I want stable emergence, better disease resistance, and a more reliable harvest. I will fertilize moderately instead of heavily, because I want enough yield but I do not want to waste money or push the crop too hard. I will irrigate wheat more carefully since spring here can turn dry, while summer maize can rely more on rainfall unless the field clearly needs water. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier for me to manage than deep ploughing and still gives a workable seedbed. I will keep pesticide spraying limited and only do the main necessary rounds, because I want to control pests and disease without overspending. If weather is normal, this is the plan I would trust most for a steady year.
